text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Acting president of the Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN), Jacob Nghifindaka accuses a number of leading Namibian mining companies of contributing to the excalating number of HIV/Aids cases in the country through the "inhuman treatment" of workers.
- Nghifindaka has called on union members to resolve to press government to change laws permitting foreigners permanent residence in Namibia.

- President Sam Nujoma has hailed the youth for its contribution to the independence of Namibia. Addressing the Swapo Youth League Congress, he called on Namibia's youth to accept the challenges arising from a new political order and take on the responsibilities of helping to find solutions to situations brought about by the changes.

- Namibia's Association of tour and safari operators has come out against what it terms vague and unfounded statements contained in a circular which is being distributed by the Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA) since March.
- Prime Minister Hage Geingob has urged the Swapo Youth League Congress to fight tribalism, nepotism and racism, and to guard against corruption.
